questions.prompt: Each DataGrid row has a Delete button with `CommandParameter="{Binding}"`. What is passed to `DeleteItemCommand`?
options: The `Transaction` object of the clicked row
questions.explanation: Inside the cell template the DataContext is the row item, so `CommandParameter="{Binding}"` passes the current row object (`Transaction`) to the command.

questions.prompt: Why do the notes prefer `DeleteItem(Transaction item)` with `CommandParameter` over `DeleteSelected()` for row actions?
options: It acts on the exact row, independent of the selection
It deletes every selected row at once in a single call
It avoids the need for any `RelativeSource` binding
It works without needing an `ICommand` implementation
questions.explanation: `DeleteSelected()` depends on the selection and is one global delete, while `DeleteItem(Transaction item)` acts on the exact row, has no dependency on selection and is cleaner MVVM.

questions.prompt: How does the lesson's `AsyncRelayCommand` stop a double-click from starting the load twice?
options: It runs `_executeAsync` on `Task.Run`, so a second click is queued
It relies on `CommandManager` to notice the click and disable the button
It ignores every click after the first for the life of the window
`CanExecute` is `false` while `_isExecuting` is set, so the button disables
questions.explanation: `CanExecute` is `!_isExecuting && ...`. `Execute` sets `_isExecuting = true` and raises `CanExecuteChanged` before awaiting, so the button is disabled while the async work runs, with no CommandManager involved.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of `AsyncRelayCommand.Execute` in order.
steps: Set `_isExecuting = true` and raise `CanExecuteChanged` (the button disables)
In `finally`, set `_isExecuting = false` and raise `CanExecuteChanged` again (the button re-enables)
questions.explanation: `Execute` guards with `CanExecute`, marks itself busy and notifies the UI, awaits the work, and in `finally` clears the flag and notifies again so the button is re-enabled even if the work fails.

questions.prompt: Which of these is listed as a common mistake when writing async commands?
options: Disabling the button while the async work runs
Exposing an `IsBusy` property for a ProgressBar
questions.explanation: The common-mistakes list includes using `CommandManager` with async commands, not disabling the button during async work, `async void` ViewModel methods, `Task.Run` for I/O and `MessageBox` in the ViewModel.
